_note: filename -> [top%, bottom%] of the FACE BAND: the top of the highest
hat or hairline to the lowest chin, as a percentage of the published
frame's height. Read by scripts/build_banners.py and published into
docs/data/church/banners.json as 'face_band'.
MEASURED OFF THE ART (2172x724) against the 280px band, per face:
left, Georgia, white hair and beard   ~15-41%   <- the highest hairline
left-centre, Virginia, blonde          ~21-46%  <- the lowest chin
centre, Texas A&M, maroon quarter-zip  ~17-42%
right-centre, Stanford, headset+beard  ~15-45%
right, Wake Forest, black polo         ~21-43%
So [15, 46]. All five stand at the same depth and are framed at the
same scale, which is why this band is 31% of frame where the browns
trophy chase -- same 3:1 crop, but with a figure kneeling a head below
the line -- needs 69% and cannot be framed at this cap at all.
The bulldog at lower left (~66-85%) is deliberately NOT in this band.
It is a mascot, not one of the five, and including it would push the
band to [15, 85] and the floor to 317px -- failing, at this cap, a
banner whose five faces it holds with 139px to spare. If the dog ever
has to be guaranteed visible that is a framing decision for focal.json
or a re-crop, not a face-band measurement.
